text:
kevin: Heads up — we're seeing a 15-30% p95 regression on small-batch text gen after the driver roll to CUDA 12.14.1 in staging. Runs on A100, batch sizes 1-4.

maria: Oof. Any repro on the perf harness? stack + exact image? :thinking:

kevin: Repro'd on perf harness. Image: rwd-infer:nightly-2026-03-16, torch 2.6.1, triton 2.4.1. Attached a short perf run: 

```
# perf harness command
./run_perf.py --model gpt-small --seq 256 --batch 1 --iters 500 --device a100
```

kevin: CPU traces show frequent kernel path switches during generation and a ton of driver-level preempt/reschedule messages in dmesg. Perf flame shows two matmul kernels alternating: matmul_tile32_opt and matmul_tile16_fallback.

samir: I pulled the KV cache profiler for the same run — observed repeated prefetch cancels and KV cache eviction/reload for the same request id. Looks correlated with when kernel selection flips.

anna: Any difference if you pin to cudnn/cuBLAS versions? or try rolling back driver?

kevin: Quick test: rollback driver to 12.14.0 on a node — small-batch p95 returns to baseline. So strong signal to the driver bump.

maria: If rollback fixes it that's great. Can we bisect driver minor? Do infra allow 12.14.1 -> 12.14.0 rollback easily?

kevin: We did a controlled node rollback. Also ran a bisect-style test across our perf CI image: toggled driver build between 12.14.0 and 12.14.1 — 12.14.1 consistently shows kernel path hysteresis and 10-30% p95 up.

samir: I dumped triton autotune tables and kernels selected per-run. On 12.14.1 the autotuner prefers tile16 kernel for smallseq on several shapes; on 12.14.0 it picks tile32. The tile16 kernel has worse latency despite similar throughput in bulk bench. Looks like driver scheduler changed preemption granularity so autotune scoring (latency heuristic) flips.

kevin: Profiling snippets:

```
# trace snippet
KERNEL_SELECT: shape=(1,256) opts=tile32 score=1.12 -> tile16 score=1.09
DRIVER_PREEMPT: preempt_timeout=80us
DRIVER_RESCHED: event=preempted pid=4523
```

anna: Is it reproducible on CPU-only runs? probably not. Any perf counters?

samir: Collected cupti counters — on 12.14.1 we see higher SM active/instr reissue ratio and increased serialization events around the matmul kernels. Also higher context-switch counts in driver tracing.

maria: Could be driver changed async preemption heuristics or introduced a new scheduling policy for compute preemption that hurts short kernels. That could push autotuner to favor lower-latency-looking kernels that actually thrash due to preemption overhead.

kevin: Agreed. Hypothesis: driver 12.14.1 reduces preemption timeout or increases preemptible quantum, which makes medium-width matmul slower under our continuous-batching workload. Autotune uses observed latency samples and flips kernel preference, leading to oscillation across requests.

anna: What do logs show during a single request? Any back-to-back kernel launches from different threads?

kevin: Logs show interleaved launches and short-lived kernels being preempted mid-execution; then a fallback kernel gets launched. Sequence: launch tile32 -> preempt -> launch tile16 -> finishes but overall more wall time.

samir: I ran a small experiment: forcing kernel hint to tile32 in the runtime bypasses autotune and removes p95 spike even on 12.14.1. So immediate mitigation: pin kernel hint for smallseq shapes.

maria: OK mitigation path: 1) Pin kernel choice for affected shapes in runtime (hotfix), 2) Roll back driver rollout in staging and ramp down, 3) Open vendor support ticket with driver team with traces and CUPTI counters, 4) Add regression test in perf CI to catch this pattern.

kevin: I'll open a PR to add a kernel-hint map for gpt-small shapes and a runtime flag to force it. Also filing infra rollback request now.

ci-bot: Deploy task created: rollback-driver-staging -> scheduled for next maintenance window.

maria: For the support ticket, collect: full dmesg with tracepoints, CUPTI perf counters, triton autotune tables, and the perf harness run. Samir can you assemble artifacts?

samir: On it. Will attach flame graphs, autotune dumps, and a short repro script.

kevin: Also adding a short perf CI job: run small-batch p95 for seq 128/256 on A100 after driver/libraries step in the CI matrix. Gate on >10% regression vs baseline.

anna: One more note: we should check dedicated nodes with mixed workloads — this change might affect throughput tail in production when we have multi-tenant small-batch traffic.

maria: Agreed. Add an alert rule for sudden small-batch p95 deltas after infra upgrades.

deploy-bot: Rollback scheduled, nodes will be drained, driver reverted to 12.14.0. ETA ~45m. :arrow_backward:

kevin: Thanks. After rollback I'll run an extended soak and then we can land the kernel-hint hotfix behind a config flag.

maria: Filing internal postmortem template and tagging infra + drivers.

kevin: Summary of action items: rollback in staging, PR to pin hint, open driver vendor ticket, add perf CI gate, alerting rule.

samir: I'll push collected artifacts to the ticket and link here when done.

kevin: TL;DR: driver 12.14.1 changed async preempt behavior -> runtime autotune picks a worse kernel -> small-batch p95 regression. Mitigations: rollback + kernel hint.
